recommendation: Keep this audit as-is for the core spec source. If tooling still permits slices on non-array, non-choice elements, track and fix that in hapifhir/org.hl7.fhir.core; do not add redundant source prose unless FHIR-I later decides the profiling rules need further normative clarification.
issue_request: FHIR-26553 was a Published/Persuasive FHIR-I technical correction raised against R4 and applied for R5. It asked that tooling prevent slices from being defined on non-array, non-choice elements, using the catalog profile's Composition.date:IssueDate slice as the example.
initial_application: No Jira-tagged HL7/fhir source commit was found for FHIR-26553. The example catalog source was later corrected implicitly by commit 445fa74909, which changed source/composition/structuredefinition-profile-catalog.xml from Composition.date:IssueDate with sliceName IssueDate to a normal Composition.date constraint retaining alias IssueDate. Current source and the built catalog profile show no Composition.date sliceName.
additional_context: The issue was created after a Zulip exchange where Grahame Grieve said the catalog sliceName was invalid and that tooling should not let it exist; FHIR-I minutes record FHIR-26553 as a technical correction. A later Jira comment by Grahame directed the remaining tooling follow-up to https://github.com/hapifhir/org.hl7.fhir.core. Current profiling/ElementDefinition narrative covers slicing around repeated entries and choice-type slicing, while the requested enforcement is validator/tooling behavior outside this HL7/fhir spec source checkout.
reconciliation: No FHIR source hunk was made. The combined branch received an empty external-repo audit commit because the current and built catalog profile no longer has the invalid Composition.date slice, and validator enforcement belongs in org.hl7.fhir.core or another tooling repository rather than in this source checkout.

related_jiras.note: Specific catalog profile Composition.date slice that exposed the tooling gap; not decided here because it is a separate OO-owned No Change tracker, and the current source already has only an alias on Composition.date.
